counterfactual_missing_items: No symptom onset within days-weeks after the October 2020 infection
No psoriasis, nail pits, or dactylitis to support PsA
No HLA-B27 or sacroiliitis imaging to support axial SpA
decisive_items: joint symptoms, followed by acute back pain and paresthesia
response.rationale: R7 is favored because the joint symptoms began 'shortly after vaccination', a proximate trigger, whereas R4 is the broad reactive arthritis category without this temporal specificity and C1 relies on a remote SARS-CoV-2 infection months earlier. Negative RF/anti-CCP and morning stiffness/multiple joint involvement favor a seronegative reactive arthritis; OA, PsA, RA, and nonspecific SpA lack key supporting features.

rejected.why: Negative RF and anti-CCP, DIP involvement, and post-vaccination onset are against RA.
No psoriasis/nail findings; Heberden node is an OA sign, not PsA; acute vaccine-related pattern unexplained.
Heberden node is present but acute inflammatory symptoms, morning stiffness, multiple joints, and post-vaccination timing are not OA.
Back pain/paresthesia is nonspecific; no inflammatory back pain criteria, HLA-B27, or sacroiliitis imaging.
Confirms SARS-CoV-2 exposure but omits the arthritis presentation and the vaccine temporal link.
